title: Filament Eruption and Its Reformation Caused by Emerging Magnetic Flux

summary.content_summary: This study observes and analyzes the eruption and reformation of a solar filament induced by emerging magnetic flux. The instruments actively used include the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST) and instruments from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) - specifically the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) and Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI). Additionally, data from the Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager (RHESSI) and Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) were utilized for complementary observations, particularly focusing on hard X-ray sources and solar flare flux. Observations also included inputs from the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph Experiment (LASCO) onboard the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) that assisted in identifying associated Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs). Data collection spanned multiple periods throughout July 15, 2013, with precise temporal coordination between instruments to study magnetic field evolution, flare activities, and the dynamic movements within the corona, directly contributing to the comprehensive understanding of the filament behaviors and their triggers.
